doc.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Her current trio and Arsenio Hall
summary: She describes Roy McCurdy, John B. Williams, Michael Wolff, Arsenio Hall and Lou Mathews, who hesitated to join until he could accompany her like Jimmy Jones.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Great. That’s what you’re going to do tonight. Tell us about your current trio. I know Roy’s been with you.

Roy [McCurdy]. Oh forever. Roy and I obviously we ran into, I know Roy from the Cannonball Adderley days. But he’s been on the road with me for sixteen years. John B. Williams, who nationally is known on the Arsenio show for five years, but he was with me for ten years before that, and Arsenio, because I’m kind of Mom to him, said, “Mom can I really” —

They got my — and Michael Wolff was not with me then but had been with me for five years. So when Arsenio was out on the road with us it was Michael Wolff, John B. Williams and Roy. So he, Mike was, he always told them, told Michael, that if something happens to me, I’m going to do this and he did and he asked. And I know that the men are real happy about that. And this is one of the most loyal people in the world is Arsenio. So I’m very happy for the guys. John B. is back, Lou Mathews, one of the best keyboard players, a magnificent conductor. As comfortable with a trio as he is with a symphony orchestra. And told me frankly, although he tried to get him for some time, that until he © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

felt that he could accompany me as well as Jimmy Jones, you know he loved what Jimmy did for me, that he and he just said I’m not ready. I don’t think I’ll—but he’s been with me now for ten years — so— but that’s the kind of feeling you want from your musicians.
